Lubycza Krolewska Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lubycza Królewska, Poland

Demolished. Lubycza Królewska's Jewish population made up an extraordinary 80 to 90 percent of the town throughout the 19th and 20th centuries, reaching 85 percent by 1939. Jews leased a mid-19th-century factory producing well-known faience pottery specifically for Jewish religious worship. This cemetery, likely founded in the second half of the 18th century, was partially destroyed during WWII, its tombstones used to pave roads; after the war, the local population destroyed the remainder, using the wall and remaining tombstones in other construction projects. In the 1980s, the site was bulldozed, a new road paved through it, and the land divided into house plots.
